title: Matt LaFleur says St. Brown's 'mentality' sets him apart
headline: LaFleur has no concern about Watson or Golden for Sunday's game at Detroit, Jordan Love's back is a watch-list item, and Zeitler is being ramped up.
summary: LaFleur was asked about Christian Watson and Matthew Golden for Sunday and said there is no concern. A "Jordan" came to the staff after the last game with a back problem. The coach said he took some shots and was seen with the chiropractor, and from context this is most likely QB Jordan Love. When asked whether Love would be limited today, LaFleur said only that the team will see on the field. Kevin Zeitler is being ramped up through the strength and athletic training staff, and the coach said the next two days of practice matter. A start decision will rest on conversations and the eyeball test. Jonathan Ford was placed on IR after playing through an issue until he couldn't. Luke Musgrave is unlikely to play this season, though LaFleur wouldn't close the door. LaFleur spent much of the session praising Detroit: Jared Goff is decisive and poised under pressure, Brian Branch is back and one of the league's best safeties, Jahmyr Gibbs is a dynamic threat as a runner and receiver, and Amon-Ra St. Brown's mentality sets him apart. He also said the practice schedule is built around getting players' bodies right rather than maximizing reps.

topics.topic: Preparing for an opponent coming off a bye
topics.detail: He said it doesn't change his approach much. Early-season-style unscripted looks are possible, so the team has to trust its rules and training.
Asked whether Musgrave will play this season, LaFleur said no until proven otherwise but wouldn't close the door.

The captions name him "Jordan Riley", a name not on the roster, so he can't be identified with confidence. LaFleur said he has shown a ton of progress, got his feet wet last week, and could be ready if the progress continues.
LaFleur called Brian Branch one of the league's best safeties. He said Branch brings physicality and toughness and is comfortable playing man-to-man on receivers.
LaFleur said the way to slow Goff is to move him off his spot and pressure him. He called Goff decisive, poised and quick to let the ball go, and said he doesn't pre-read throws.

LaFleur said defenders must keep their leverage and never relax against a back who can reverse field and score. He described Gibbs as a threat out of the backfield who could line up at slot receiver for most teams.
LaFleur said St. Brown can run any route, but his mentality and mindset set him apart from most players, calling him "a dog".

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 22, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley could return this week, but Sirianni gave no firm timeline; Tanner McKee is the full-week starter at QB while Jalen Hurts' blood clot situation stays off the table.
summary: Sirianni praised Saquon Barkley as a phenomenal player and captain and said he was looking forward to seeing him on the field at practice. He kept his status open, saying only that they will see where he is as the week goes on. He said adding a back of Barkley's caliber would be a huge plus, and he credited the backs who stepped in while the room was beat up. He said Tanner McKee has the intelligence, toughness and work ethic to keep rising, and that every rep counts as he gets a full week of work as the starter. Sirianni declined to discuss Jalen Hurts' medical situation, how often Hurts will be around the team, the NFLPA's call for an investigation, or the $250,000 fine. He said he misses Hurts and that the situation is fluid. He said the offense will stay flexible, with players over plays, and that the team has to get back on track after losing four in a row. On Zach Ertz, he said he is still with the team, is out of practice-squad elevations, has practiced well, and has looked great with the ones and on the scout team. He said he loves having Ertz but can't predict what comes next. He also covered facing Cowboys DC Christian Parker, a former Eagles assistant. He said familiarity helps both sides, but week-to-week film and putting a seed of doubt in the defense matter more.

injuries.detail: Sirianni was looking forward to seeing him at practice and said they will see where he is as the week progresses. No timeline was given, but the comments suggest he is possibly returning to practice.
Sirianni declined to discuss the blood clot situation. He said recovery timelines vary and his involvement with the team is fluid.

signals.quote: every rep counts and every rep matters.

signals.note: Sirianni would not share details on Hurts' timeline or involvement, so he is not a near-term fantasy option.
signals.quote: I miss Jaylen, miss being around him on a daily basis.

signals.note: Ertz has looked good in practice but is not in a set game role. Sirianni gave no promise of promotion.
signals.quote: I love having Zach on this football team.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the offense is built on players over plays, and the scheme will adapt to the opponent and the team's strengths. The run game, third-down conversions and manageable situations drive the play-action game.

Parker previously worked on the Eagles' defensive staff. Sirianni said he did not sit in offensive meetings, and the two teams have so much film on each other that the key is planting a seed of doubt in the defense.
The Eagles have lost four straight and Sirianni said they need to get back on track. He also said he still enjoys coaching and is working to grow as a coach and person.
Sirianni declined to discuss the $250,000 fine or his conversations with the league and referees.
